title: FWKV: A Fixed-Decay Recurrent Architecture with Token Shift and Convolutional Scan
summary: FWKV is a recurrent language model architecture that replaces self-attention with per-channel fixed-decay recurrences. Decays are initialized across timescales from 2 to 1000 tokens, the recurrence is evaluated as an fp32 FFT convolution during training and as a fixed-size state update during generation, and token shift, unit-gain inputs, and per-head normalization stabilize each block. The paper gives the full forward equations, the equivalence between training and inference forms, and complexity analysis, with no custom kernels or positional encodings required.

title: FWKV: Simplicity Is All You Need for Efficient Language Modeling
summary: The FWKV family of recurrent language models (29M–56M params) achieves up to 48.1 tok/s on CPU via a fixed-decay accumulator computed with an O(log T) vectorized parallel scan, eliminating both quadratic attention and the KV cache. The architecture pairs this recurrent core with a parameter-free suffix-automaton copy mechanism (ROSA) for exact long-range copying, and requires no custom CUDA kernels, no gating, and no position embeddings. Models are available under Apache 2.0.
